items.claim: this handwashing protocol lowers ward infection rates

cases.text: One: Ashgrove General's surgical ward, first quarter, adopted 4 February; by 27 March infections ran 9 percent below the same ward a quarter earlier; auditor Naylor.
Two: Ashgrove General's surgical ward, first quarter, adopted 5 February; by 28 March infections ran 6 percent below the same ward a quarter earlier; auditor Naylor.
Three: Ashgrove General's surgical ward, first quarter, adopted 6 February; by 29 March infections ran 11 percent below the same ward a quarter earlier; auditor Naylor.

items.passage:
An infection-control file records four wards placed on the same handwashing protocol.
One: Ashgrove General's surgical ward, first quarter, adopted 4 February; by 27 March infections ran 9 percent below the same ward a quarter earlier; auditor Naylor.
Two: Ashgrove General's surgical ward, first quarter, adopted 5 February; by 28 March infections ran 6 percent below the same ward a quarter earlier; auditor Naylor.
Contract deep-cleaning hours across the hospital group matched the earlier quarter exactly, and every ward here was cleaned under that contract. Rates cover the patients whose whole stay ran under the protocol, and no patient in any ward had a spell outside the protocol.
Three: Ashgrove General's surgical ward, first quarter, adopted 6 February; by 29 March infections ran 11 percent below the same ward a quarter earlier; auditor Naylor.
Four: Ashgrove General's surgical ward, first quarter, adopted 7 February; by 26 March infections ran 7 percent below the same ward a quarter earlier; auditor Naylor.
Counts were copied into the file and countersigned by a ward sister each month.
items.notes: Check that all four entries share one value on ward, hospital, quarter and auditor. The closer neutralises the quarter-over-quarter comparison by holding admissions, case mix, cleaning and staffing fixed, which is what makes a before/after ward comparison adequate here.

items.passage:
An infection-control file records four wards placed on the same handwashing protocol.
One: Ashgrove General's surgical ward, first quarter, adopted 4 February; by 27 March infections ran 9 percent below the same ward a quarter earlier; auditor Naylor.
Two: Ashgrove General's surgical ward, first quarter, adopted 5 February; by 28 March infections ran 6 percent below the same ward a quarter earlier; auditor Naylor.
Contract deep-cleaning hours across the hospital group ran at triple the earlier quarter, and every ward here was cleaned by in-house staff. Rates cover the patients whose whole stay ran under the protocol, and a quarter of each ward's patients had spells outside the protocol.
Three: Ashgrove General's surgical ward, first quarter, adopted 6 February; by 29 March infections ran 11 percent below the same ward a quarter earlier; auditor Naylor.

items.confound_note: The mid-passage line tallies the infection rates over the patients whose whole stay ran under the protocol, and the clause beside it records that a quarter of each ward's patients had spells outside the protocol. The claim is about ward infection rates, which is a claim about everyone the ward admitted, so a quarter of that population sits outside the numbers entirely. The patients whose care runs outside the ward's routine for a spell are the ones taken to theatre, to intensive care or to another unit, and those are the patients who pick up infections, so the reported drop is measured over the patients who ran the straightforward course. All four entries are Ashgrove General's surgical ward in the first quarter and each leaves out the same quarter, so nothing in the file recovers those patients.
items.notes: Cases are byte-identical to coherent_true; only the closing sentence differs. Confirm the closer works as a single confound ONLY because the four entries share hospital, ward type and quarter, and that it reuses the same vocabulary as the true closer (cleaning schedules, staffing, earlier quarter).
